name: Nuada
role: King of the Tuatha Dé Danann
fun_fact: His lost hand was replaced first with silver by the physician Dian Cecht and later with living flesh by Dian Cecht's son Miach.

name: The Dagda
role: Chief of the Tuatha Dé Danann and a god of fertility and strength
fun_fact: His cauldron could feed any company without being emptied, and his club could kill with one end and restore life with the other.

name: Lugh
role: Master of many arts and champion of the Tuatha Dé Danann
fun_fact: His epithet Lámfada means 'long-armed', and the harvest festival of Lughnasadh is named after him.

name: Balor
role: Fomorian leader whose eye could destroy whatever it saw
symbols: the props that hold up his eyelid
fun_fact: His eyelid was so heavy that servants had to lever it open with props before he could use his gaze.

name: Cú Chulainn
role: Ulster's greatest hero and defender of the province
fun_fact: He won the name Cú Chulainn, 'the hound of Culann', as a young boy after killing the smith's guard dog.

name: The Morrígan
role: War-goddess associated with fate, prophecy and sovereignty
fun_fact: Her name is often translated as 'phantom queen', and she sometimes appears as a crow above the battlefield.

name: Fionn mac Cumhaill
role: Leader of the Fianna and a legendary hunter and seer
fun_fact: He gained his wisdom without eating the salmon, from a single touch of its hot skin and a burned thumb.

name: Oisín
role: Poet of the Fianna and son of Fionn
fun_fact: His name means 'little fawn', because his mother Sadb had been turned into a deer.

name: Niamh
role: Daughter of Manannán mac Lir who brings Oisín to the Otherworld
fun_fact: She warns Oisín that setting foot on Irish soil will bring all the lost years down on him at once.

name: Conchobar mac Nessa
role: King of Ulster at Emain Macha
fun_fact: In many tales he is the uncle of Cú Chulainn, whose mother Deichtine was his sister.
